data.body: EVIDENCE (close): Gerrit change 2149 MERGED as 5b1ef1157c2883550716b3cde4798c89ead9f593 (LLM-Review +1 by rebar review bot, Verified +1 by rebar CI bot, 0 unresolved; 6 advisory findings, non-blocking). LIVE BEFORE/AFTER LOCK-HOLD (this host, live store ~5,300 tickets, multi-session load): BEFORE the drain lock was held across the whole batch incl. LLM calls — 437s and 131s observed holds for <=5-item batches (design comment on draughty-callous-tanager). AFTER (instrumented in-process drain of the merged build, real LLM): lock held 196.7s for a 20-item claim window with ZERO LLM time under the lock, then 19/20 items enriched lock-free — per-item lock cost 87.4s -> 9.8s (~9x), and the hung-provider-wedges-every-drainer failure class is gone entirely (a stuck LLM call now blocks only its own batch). The residual collect hold on the live store is dominated by the two full-store walks (drainer census + stale-digest self-heal) and 20 claim appends/pushes under multi-session push contention — scratch-store collect was 1.5-2.9s (E2), so live push contention is the driver; that is the dedicated-clone follow-on territory the design deliberately deferred. THROUGHPUT (OQ2): backlog already draining through normal traffic — pending 1,046 at design time -> 970 now, with 22 live claims from concurrent drainers (old single-flight: 5 items per multi-minute exclusive hold; new: up to 3 concurrent drainers x 20-item batches, collect-only lock). Enqueue sources (certifications + self-heal) run well under that service rate. All 9 ACs ticked in the description; mechanism pins live in tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py.
